text: A BLAST search returns a hit with an E-value of 1e-3. How should this result typically be interpreted?
choices: Highly significant homology, near certainty of a true evolutionary relationship
Borderline; conventionally not considered significant since common thresholds are around 1e-5 or lower
The alignment covers exactly 0.1% of the query sequence length
The probability that the two sequences are homologous is precisely 0.001
explanation: An E-value of 1e-3 falls short of the conventional significance threshold of about 1e-5 (with 1e-10 considered high-confidence), so it is generally treated as borderline rather than significant. The E-value is the expected number of chance hits at that score, not a probability of homology and not a measure of query coverage, so the last two options misinterpret what the statistic means.
